what: Waters makes the instruments laboratories use to find out exactly what is in a sample: liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry systems, the columns and chemicals they consume, and the software that runs them.
customers: Pharmaceutical and biotech laboratories above all, plus food safety, environmental and materials testing labs.
money: columns, reagents and service contracts bought repeatedly
moat: Instruments validated into regulated drug-manufacturing processes, which cannot be swapped without re-validation, and the consumables that only work with them.
risks: Pharmaceutical customers cut instrument spending sharply in downturns
Chinese demand has been weak and is subject to government stimulus decisions
The combination with Becton Dickinson's biosciences unit is a large integration
Reported net income was depressed by one-off items in the last period
opportunities: Recurring consumables and service revenue is over half of sales and far steadier than instruments
Regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing requires continuous testing regardless of the economic cycle
Replacement demand builds after several weak instrument years
watch: Instrument orders, which lead revenue, and recurring revenue growth.
